Contains information about supported file types for example. You are able to create your own custom platform configuration in [Settings] > [Advanced] > [Custom platform configuration] > [Create].
Retroarch requires a path to the emulator core: For example \'/data/data/com.retroarch/cores/ppsspp_libretro_android.so\'.

Most apps don\'t require an explicit Activity, so you can usually leave it on [Unspecified]. However, some apps need to be targeted with an explicit Activity: Look out for fitting names like \'EmulationActivity\'.

Usually Emulators want to be pointed directly to a \'Game file\'. For some platforms however, there is not just a single file which can be pointed to. In such cases, Emulators often reference to a game through a \'Game ID\' instead (e.g. Vita3K, ScummVM).

The selected platform configuration above does not include an ID file type specification. You can create your own custom platform configuration and add a file type with a specification on how to get the game ID. Go to [Settings] > [Advanced] > [Custom platform configuration] > [Create] to create it.\nYou can still continue to set up this configuration here and save it. You can even try launching a game, but it will most likely fail because I don\'t know where to get game\'s ID from.

The standard intent action to open a document is \'android.intent.action.VIEW\' which is used by most emulation apps. In rare cases a custom action is used: E.g. for Yuzu based emulators, it is \'android.nfc.action.TECH_DISCOVERED\'.
The standard way to pass an ID to another app is through the DATA parameter. Some emulators require the file to be sent through a custom parameter however.
Usually, the ID is passed over as a Text type (\'String\'). If the ID is a number, it is possible that it is explicitly passed a Number type (\"Integer\') though.

The standard intent action to open a file is \'android.intent.action.VIEW\' which is used by most emulation apps. In rare cases a custom action is used: E.g. for Yuzu based emulators, it is \'android.nfc.action.TECH_DISCOVERED\'.
The standard way to pass a file to another app is through the DATA parameter. Some emulators require the file to be sent through a custom parameter however.
Modern apps usually refer to a file through a \'content URI\'. Older apps might use an \'absolute URL\': A hint could be that they use the \'READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE\' permission.

All changes of the stable Papaya versions at a glance.
The release notes of alpha and beta versions can be found in the Papaya Discord.
Contains features which are planned to be added after the recently released 1.0.0 version. Each section is listed by priority.
This does not mean that they are being developed strictly in this order and it’s also not a 100% promise that all of these features will come.
Bugs and shortcomings which need to be addressed
Features which have a relatively small complexity
Features with a larger complexity and are usually included in a major version
These are not planned yet, but I want to make them visible already

Support legacy paths for specific cores which do not support content URIs yet (e.g. FB Alpha 2012) and potentially add an option to force the legacy path for all cores to keep the history and save data in RA clean. Display implications of this setting („Does not support launching games from SD Card“).
After starting up Papaya, a bug causes the category selection sometimes to jump from Games to Settings.
Main screen is not properly updated when navigating back via Home button

When Papaya is set as the Launcher, you can always return to it through the Home button or Home gesture. In some edge cases when you edit a setting and then return to the main screen through the Home button (instead of back navigation), the main screen misses the update and displays an outdated state.
When the device is connected and used with a physical keyboard, the TextFields are losing the focus when a letter is typed. Workaround found by a user: Holding down the enter key 😄
Improve the scrolling animations and scrolling via touch.

In the platform configurator, display a „Get it on PlayStore“ etc. link on supported emulators which are not installed yet. When clicking on it, you’ll be directly lead to the source and can download and install it immediately. This simplifies the setup for people new to the scene as well.
Or provide a way to explicitly use the app icon instead.
Currently, you can only add as many as you want, but can’t delete them.

Currently, the importer selects the first emulator match as a game’s emulator. In some cases you will then end up with the „wrong“ match and need to change it manually after importing (E.g. PPSSPP instead of PPSSPP Gold). To improve this, Papaya should match the emulator selection against the installed apps.\n\nWhen the importer is used, it will always create new platforms for all detected ES-DE systems. If the systems are imported multiple times, Papaya will create duplicated platforms for them. Instead, each imported platform should be linked 1:1 to an ES-DE system. The importer should rather update already existing platforms.
Display amount of games in a section
Can be easily combined with the index of the currently selected game to see how far you have scrolled.
Let Papaya pick a random game for you. An idea could be to introduce this as a sorting method (like „by platform“, „by release date“) where you will then see 3-5 randomly picked games.

You should be able to quickly jump to the next letter within a section to quick scroll through a larger list. This could become more complex because of the paging mechanism: To keep the RAM usage of Papaya lightweight and to reduce loading times, Papaya loads only the first X items of a section. More are only loaded when scrolling to the end.
The hints at the bottom of the screen which tell you what the different buttons do should be clickable via touch and trigger the specific action.

Sorting options like „by platform“, „by release date“ etc. should be toggleable (enabled/disabled) and you should be able to, well, sort them. Especially when the list of sorting options grows larger: „by genre“, „by franchise“, „by collections“, „by play time“ etc.
Allow touch gestures (left/right) to change between sections in the Gallery Grid and Gallery List layouts.

Curate your games in your own lists like „My favourite childhood games“, „Super Mario“ etc. This will include a new settings screen to manage the collections (similar to platforms) with a search function to quickly find all games to add. Also, you should be able to sort your library by your collections (like by platform, by release date etc): „My favourite childhood games“ and „Super Mario“ would appear as sections. Each custom collection should have a customisable appearance: icon/logo, name, short name.
Select custom sounds for the background music, selection, back navigation etc. in a new settings menu which can be entered from the „Appearance & behaviour“ settings.

Display backgrounds and logos for games. This requires scraping these images from the scraper services and importing them from ES-DE. Plus, the manual scraping screen needs to be revamped to support selecting them individually.
Select/Unselect the apps which should appear in the Streaming category.

When Papaya is launched for the first time, it automatically detects game apps. However you currently need to manually select later installed games. Papaya should provide the option to detect new games on a button click and an automatic detection.

You should be able to customise the background animations more to your liking: Pick different colors than the accent color and modify some parameters (e.g. wavelength, speed of the waves, bubble size etc.).
Enter a search term and quickly look up games. Potentially extend this feature with a web search etc.
Request the permission to track app usage statistics (Optional) to estimate the play time of all games/apps. Potentially add the option to sort all games by play time.

Currently, app shortcuts are only supported for streaming apps and in the app options menu if Papaya is set as the Launcher. There should be a proper integration of app shortcuts in the games category: For example, you should be able to pin GameHub and Eden shortcuts to Papaya. When pinning the shortcut, you should be able to select the platform you want to add it to. E.g. GameHub shortcuts to a PC platform, Eden shortcuts to a Switch platform.

There should be a way to copy existing configurations, so you can quickly adapt to emulator changes. E.g. If PPSSPP suddenly requires an extra parameter, you could copy Papaya’s PPSSPP config, easily add the parameter and save it as a custom config. Also, the current editor is useful for people which need some guidance, but it’s also too restrictive in some scenarios. There should be an advanced mode which allows entering ADB commands.

Support exporting/importing the whole Papaya configuration. The biggest challenge will be to properly guide you during the import: The same/similar folders need to be selected again by you, so Papaya gains the permission to read the same Roms again. Papaya should communicate mismatches and provide fallbacks.

Similar to sort by platform, by release date etc. Considered a bigger feature because the genre information from the various scrapers needs to be aligned, because menus to manage that information need to be created and the info needs to be imported from ES-DE properly.
Adding a dedicated space which provides an overview over all your trophies. Plus, integrating it into other screens like the game category, game options etc.
Similar to game sections, you should be able to sort your apps to your liking. You should also be able to mark certain apps as favourites so they appear in a quick access menu.

Similar to sort by platform, by release date etc. Same complexity reasons like the „Sort by genre“ feature, but with the extra challenge that not all scrapers provide this info. In a perfect world, you should then be able to use the quick sort function to see sections like „Grand Theft Auto“ containing all GTA games across all platforms.

Please let me know what kind of themes you would like to see. There have been requests for an XBOX 360 like theme for example. The themes do not have to be based on any original and could be something completely new.
Please let me know what kind of animations you would like to see.

A separate home tab/section. This can be potentially a place to display the recents/favourites section, your recently unlocked Retro Achievements, favourite apps, recommended games and game apps (optional) and more.
If you want to, you should be able to log in with your Discord account to share your currently played game with your friends.

Currently Papaya only supports selecting the different screens where an app/game should be launched on. When Papaya is opened on a Dual Screen device, the not focused second screen could display some additional information (Game cover, logo, Retro Achievements etc). The priority of this feature is low, because there are other Frontends with that specific focus and the effort is bigger to integrate this nicely: What information is useful to be displayed? Avoiding duplicate information etc.

Some devices don’t support the Google Play Services and some people don’t want to use any Google services. There should be a way to buy Papaya outside the Google ecosystem. Supporters who bought the app in Google Play should be able to retrieve the degoogled APK as well without paying a second time.
There could be a repository with the theme API and some theme samples. Anybody who is familiar with Kotlin and Jetpack Compose could easily contribute their own themes that way.
Alternative version with libretro cores included

Not sure if that is feasible though. This is „shooting for the stars“ material. It would be neat to download libretro cores on demand and have them directly integrated in Papaya. However, there are lots of things to consider: Due to the licenses, this Papaya version would probably need to be free and supporters definitely need to receive something extra. Also, there must be proper settings to configure the cores, manage saves etc.

Papaya processes information about the installed Apps on your device. Additionally, when you explicitly grant Papaya access to certain folders on your device, it will also process metadata of the files located inside this folder (file name, folder name).

Papaya uses the information about the installed Apps on your device solely for displaying the App lists on the Home screen and for guiding you when you set up shortcuts to games inside these Apps (Preselecting installed Apps). This data is not shared with any third party and is only stored locally on your device.

The aforementioned metadata of files in certain folders you grant Papaya explicitly access to, is used to enrich the shortcuts to games in other Apps: The file names or folder names might be sent to api.igdb.com, thegamesdb.net, steamgriddb.com and/or rawg.io in exchange for more details about the game shortcut. Such details include cover images, release dates, genres etc. This additional data is again only used to display them on your Home screen. Please note that this file metadata might only be shared with one of these four services mentioned above.

Papaya stores your personal data (Installed Apps, file metadata) on your device. You can erase all of your personal data via Android\'s App settings menu: Long click Papaya\'s App icon, select "App Info", click "storage & cache" and finally "clear storage". Note: Uninstalling the App might not necessarily remove your personal data if a backup option is enabled.

If you have more questions about your personal data and its usage, you can send me an Email: mail@sebschaef.com.
